title: Ember Run
summary: The Choir's lamp-ring burns real flame on the cold rim nights, and the Hollow is out of honest heat. Solder is selling a banked reactor brick — a fist-sized orange coal that will warm a whole ring of lamps for a winter — if it arrives before it cools. Double pay, one clock, and your bike will carry the glow like a second tail-light.

objectives.label: Lift the ember brick warm from the Crusher's bank-bed
Set it in the warming hearth on the temple steps — before it goes dark

offer.text: Okay, so. Idea. The Crusher's bank-bed keeps fist-sized slugs of reactor brick at just-under-molten — the Yards call them embers, miners' heat, two hundred years of slumbering warmth, BUT they cool in about three minutes once you lift them. Always just slag foot-warmers. Useless.

Unless. UNLESS somebody fast — the fastest, specifically verified fastest person I personally know — could carry one to the Hollow before it goes dark. The choir's lamp-ring burns real flame on cold nights, they're out of honest heat, and a warm brick will kindle a hearth for a whole winter. I priced the run. You'll want to sit — no, stand, you'll want to ALREADY BE MOVING.

accept.text: Cradle's bolted behind your seat, it's braced, it's vented, it GLOWS, I may have made it glow extra because it's beautiful. Don't brake hard — embers slosh. Technically. Emotionally. GO. Clock is the brick, the brick is the clock.
Why is the pay double the normal rate?
Because Pyke said 'warm cargo owes warm margins' and Aunt Vertex cried a little and called it scripture. The Yards are a proud people. RIDE.

complete.text: The horn lit before the hearth did, did you hear? You crossed the rim and the whole ring of lamps stood UP. A hundred and sixty seconds and it went in the hearth *still cherry*. Pyke says margins like yours are why the old couriers wrote oaths instead of receipts.
The brick sang the last stretch. Low. Almost happy.
Everything warm sings if you carry it right. That's not engineering. That's — okay, it's engineering presented poetically. Tell the Choir the Yards says the winter's on us.
